speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the current policy when charging a patient who chooses to stay at different classes of a general ward during each period of stay at a public hospital; and (b) whether a patient can choose to stay at different classes of a general ward when admitted to a public hospital and be charged the respective fee of each type of class.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: For cases where some of the patients who upgrade, but they are not financially very strong, is it possible for them to appeal not to pay for the entire duration at the higher ward class, if they select just after the operation?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: The second supplementary question is, many a time, my residents tell me, when they are in the higher ward class in the previous hospitalisation period, and when they get to the next round of hospitalisation and they request a downgrade, they are often not allowed to.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: The only time they can escape this is when they are admitted to the Accident and Emergency (A&E), then they can go to a lower ward class.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Member asked, for those who upgrade, later on in their stay, can they appeal.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Of course, everyone has the right to appeal, but having said that we are trying to stop a certain behaviour, which we do not think is right.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When a patient medically requires isolation, we will isolate them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And if they have chosen a lower ward class to start with and then require isolation, they will be given higher subsidies, not withstanding being in the isolation ward.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think the specific cases the Member might have come across, might be a case where they did not manage to meet the means testing criteria.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I would like the Minister to confirm – because I have gotten feedback from some residents that when they want to downgrade from a higher ward class to a lower ward class, they are told that even after the downgrade, they will have to pay the price for the medicine of the higher ward class.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It was covered in my reply just now.
